current vendor manual; documents both the newer REST API and, for several endpoints, the equivalent classic webservice.php?operation=... call. Found lookup this way (a 13th webservice.php operation not previously modelled)

vendor source of vtigercrm 8.4.0 (GitLab archive via code.vtiger.com/api/v4). The authoritative operation registry: modules/Users/DefaultDataPopulator.php vtws_addOperationInfo() (15 core ops with params and GET/POST type), modules/Migration/schema/540_to_600RC.php (retrieve_inventory), 660_to_700.php (relatedtypes, retrieve_related, query_related; convertlead's params corrected to one encoded element), 701_to_710.php (add_related), 720_to_730.php (files_retrieve), and pkg/vtiger/modules/Mobile/modules/Mobile/Mobile.php (eleven mobile.* POST ops). Response shapes from the handlers in include/Webservices/*.php. OperationManager reads an operation's parameters only from $_GET or $_POST according to its registered type; vtws_logout() additionally rejects any method but POST.

notes: No official machine-readable spec exists for the Vtiger CRM Webservices API. The API is RPC-style: every call targets a single /webservice.php endpoint and selects an action via an `operation` param (query string for GET, x-www-form-urlencoded body for POST), with all responses wrapped in a {success, result} / {success, error} envelope. This OpenAPI 3.0.3 doc was hand-authored from Vtiger's vendor docs and cross-checked against the adaptor's compiled source. To make the RPC surface mockable, each operation is modelled as a distinct path segment under /webservice.php (these synthetic sub-paths do not literally exist upstream). The @openfn/language-vtiger adaptor itself only defines three operations: login (a getchallenge->login handshake using accessKey = md5(challengeToken + userAccessKey)), listTypes, and a generic postElement({ operation, elementType, element }) that JSON.stringifies the element and can drive create/update/revise/delete; it has no generic path builder, but postElement sends any `operation` as a POST form to webservice.php, so every POST operation, and every GET one whose params are optional, is reachable through it. Coverage (2026-11-25: 35 operations): every webservice.php operation vtigercrm 8.4.0's source registers (22 core operations plus the bundled Mobile module's eleven mobile.*), lookup from the Vtiger Cloud manual, and listtypes in both methods (GET as registered, POST as the adaptor sends it). Until 2026-11-25 the spec held the 13 operations the manual names, missing extendsession, relatedtypes, retrieve_related, query_related, add_related, retrieve_inventory, files_retrieve, convertlead, changePassword, deleteUser and the mobile.* set; reading the registry also showed logout was modelled as GET, which vtws_logout() rejects (OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED), so it is now POST. Operations are tagged Session/Metadata/Records/Query/Relations/Files/Users/Mobile rather than sharing one webservice.php group. Marked coverage:full/best-effort rather than left unclaimed: re-checked against the current vendor manual (2026-09-14), which confirms these 12 plus a 13th, lookup, documented there as also reachable via webservice.php. The newer Basic-Auth REST API (/restapi/v1/vtiger/default) the same manual describes is a different, unreachable surface (see attempts) and stays out of scope. Reusable component schemas that seed collections: Element (generic CRM record), Contact, Account, Lead, ModuleType, Field/FieldType, plus result shapes ChallengeResult, LoginResult, ListTypesResult, DescribeResult, DeleteResult, QueryResult, SyncResult and Error. Caveats: response result shapes for logout/listtypes/describe/sync are under-documented by the vendor and were synthesized from typical Vtiger behaviour; the cloud base host pattern (https://{instance}.od1.vtiger.com) is a placeholder since the adaptor accepts an arbitrary hostUrl and appends /webservice.php. Path keys (2026-11-14): every operation is the one URL /webservice.php selected by its `operation` parameter (query string for GET, form body for POST), so each is keyed /webservice.php#operation=<name>, the registry's query-discriminator convention (as azure-storage's #comp=...), instead of the earlier pseudo-paths /webservice.php/<name>, which no real request ever hits. Vtiger lower-cases the operation name server-side; the adaptor sends listTypes, which the spec keys as the documented listtypes. ModuleType no longer requires `name` (2026-11-14): listtypes' information map is keyed by module name and its entries carry isEntity/label/singular only, as openfn-mocker's conformance run surfaced.
